## Short description

<!--
Please describe your implementation and any details that we should keep in mind during review.

This updates the `Toast` component so that its auto dismiss effect is compatible with new `<StrictMode>` behaviours in dev mode. As we can no longer assume effects are just run once, this removes the `timeoutRunning` state, reducing the reliance on the `setupAutoDismiss` effect and instead allow `startTimeout` to set the timeout directly.

### Test plan

* Run storybook and navigate to http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/design-system-toast--notification-toasts-story. 
* [ ] Verify that toasts are dismissed after 10s
* [ ] Verify that hovering your mouse over the toasts prevents it from auto dismissing, and moving the cursor off restarts the timeout
* [ ] Optional: we can't test Reactist's storybook in React 18 without upgrading Storybook, so we can follow the instructions on using yelc to run this within Todoist, specifically [this branch](https://github.com/Doist/todoist-web/pull/13388) where we boot React with `createRoot`

author: rhewett-nv
body:
This PR greatly improves usability if the inprocess fault injection testing tool.

* Adds a workload exception, which can be raised directly by the workload, without the violence of an async exception.  This is useful for testing specific scenarios, as the async exception will randomly interrupt and can hit unrecoverable operations.  Using this requires a slight modification to the workload.
* Separates the actual injection call logic from the setup logic.  With this, workloads can have their own setup logic but still invoke the provided call logic.
* Improved registration of possible injected faults.  External workloads can now register their own faults and use the same logic to inject it.

author: dannf
body:
This catches us up with my current tree: https://github.com/dannf/ldso-cache/commits/devel/. The really important bit here is https://github.com/chainguard-dev/apko/pull/1665/commits/d6b89ebf202d8176f11113846c0ad705dbaa21da, which fixes a bug that can cause libraries to not be found at runtime even though they are in the cache because `ld` apparently requires them to be sorted.

It also does away with an optimization I had where it would not add a library to the cache if it had already added a library with the same name from a different directory. I had done this to replicate `ldconfig`'s behavior, but I misunderstood that behavior. `ldconfig` does add multiple libs of the same name to the cache. But it does seem to detect when 2 libs are actually the same file (e.g. /lib/libfoo.so.4 and /usr/lib/libfoo.so.4 when /lib -> /usr/lib). I think a better answer for us would be to just stop listing symlinked dirs in `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/*` snippets.

Also, this finally adds testing for the file scanning logic using a mock elf parser.
